why: Transylvanian-Ottoman diplomacy in the prince's own cipher; monoalphabetic and nearly complete, so a ciphertext-only break is plausible.
verify: Find the record in the E 190 database and any image; try monoalphabetic solution in Hungarian.
access_note: MNL OL E 190 database (descriptions, no page images located)

links.label: Lang 2015, Titkosirás a kora ujkori Magyarországon (MTA doctoral thesis, repertory pp. 191-330), p. 263

vetting_note: Ciphertext not seen (MNL OL E 190 43. doboz 5. tetel no. 597 is not imaged; the MNL database has no image) and a printed clear may exist: Szilagyi, Levelek es okiratok I. Rakoczy Gyorgy keleti osszekottetesei tortenetehez (1883, REAL-EOD 6176) no. 10, Rakoczi to Racz, Udvarhely 27 Apr 1642, pp. 665-668 (PDF pages 671-674), says 'Az czifrakkal valo irast magyarra megforditattuk ... megkuldtuk' and prints as its enclosure the Hungarian text of the cipher letter of Sebes, 19 Jan 1642, from Rakoczi's draft and a contemporary copy of the cipher ('A cursivval szedett egy egykoru masolat titkos irasabol van'). Racz (letters of 4 Mar and 15 May 1642, ibid. and Beke-Barabas 1888 pp. 583-585) could not read 'ket clavissal irt' letters (a reciprocal half-alphabet: 'az felso rend betuket az alsokon ... kell erteni') and sent them back, which is why a letter to Racz sits in the Rakoczi archive. Needs an image of no. 597 (MNL reading room or reproduction order) to compare with Szilagyi pp. 667-668 before any verdict; Lang 2015 p. 263 calls it 'nincs feltorve'.

title: Count of Monterrey, the Constable of Castile and Francisco de Borja → the Duke of Villahermosa: letters in four ciphers, several with period translations
correspondents: Count of Monterrey; Constable of Castile; Francisco de Borja → Duke of Villahermosa (governor of the Spanish Netherlands from 1675)
folio_note: Folios approximate unless read. Pairs with a period clear in vol. 1 (Mss/2408): Monterrey, Brussels 30 Mar 1674, ff. 190-191v and a second ciphered copy, with 'Copia de carta de S.E. ... [desci]frada por el Duque, Brujas a 1.o de abril 1674' (ff. 192-193v, read); Monterrey, Brussels 8 Apr 1674 (clear f. 249, read) and 14 Apr 1674 ('Copia de carta ...'); Monterrey, Aranjuez 8 May 1675, clear in the margin (f. 139v); Constable, Madrid 11 Sep 1675, separate translation (f. 118, read). Borja, Madrid 1679 (both vols.): marginal glosses on part of the blocks only (about 15-30 % of the cipher). Ciphered with no clear seen: Monterrey 1674 (about ff. 175-177, 247-248, 260-263, 273-288, 330-338), Constable (vol. 1 f. 50; vol. 2 ff. 66, 79, 100-101, 107, 113-114 and two long runs), Monterrey 1675 (ff. 147-149), Borja 20 Dec 1673 (vol. 2 ff. 1-3) and 1679 (vol. 1 ff. 375-377). Group counts are rough visual estimates.
status: From the printed BNE Inventario general. Views checked on thumbnails and close-ups, 4 Nov 2026. The pairs listed in folio_note are period decipherments or translations (existing). Four systems, none of them the one of Mss/2043: Monterrey, Brussels 1674 (numbers 1-3 digits with isolated letter-signs, struck-through numbers probably nulls); Constable, Madrid 1673-75 (1-2 digit numbers with vowel-consonant digraphs); Monterrey, Madrid/Aranjuez 1675 (numbers with written syllables); Borja, Madrid 1673 and 1679 (dotted numbers with a nomenclator in thousands). The Inventario's 'Monterrey 1674 (siege of Oudenaarde) con su traduccion', 'Borja 18 Apr 1679 con su traduccion' and 'Constable 25 Oct 1673 con su traduccion' were not found as such. Rough extent left in cipher with no clear seen: 5,000-7,000 groups (Monterrey 1674), 3,000-4,000 (Constable), about 700 (Monterrey 1675), about 1,300 (Borja). No key built yet.
why: The Madrid court and the governor in Brussels writing in cipher during the Dutch War (1673-79); the period translations can give four keys for the letters left unread.
score_note: Scored from the Inventario general and a thumbnail pass with close-ups, 4 Nov 2026 (research/dudout_leads_2026-11-04/, issue #254)
verify: Rebuild the Monterrey 1674 key from the 30 Mar 1674 pair (two ciphered copies of the same text) and test it on 8 and 14 Apr; then the Constable key from 11 Sep 1675; read the letters with no clear.
prior_art: open as far as checked (4 Nov 2026: catalogue.json and research/leads.json have no Mss/2408, 2409, Villahermosa, Constable, Monterrey 1674 or Borja 1673/79 entry; three web text searches found no edition or study of these ciphered letters). Vols. 3-8 of the series were not looked at and may hold other translations.

title: Short ciphered biglietto (c. 13r) in the Medici letters of Ginori Conti 29.137, cc. 1-39
correspondents: Medici circle (Lorenzo de' Medici / Niccolo Michelozzi correspondence of 1481)
shelfmark: Florence, Biblioteca nazionale centrale, Ginori Conti 29.137 (cc. 1-39) (Manus CNMD record 611145)
status: Existing (edition), probable (Brice Dudout, 5 Nov 2026): the 1964 Censimento of Lorenzo's letters lists two Lorenzo to Michelozzi pieces in GC 29.137 (July? and 5 Aug 1481), so Lettere VI (1481-82) very likely prints this biglietto. Not checked in the volume. Earlier note: Manus: 'Il biglietto e in scrittura cifrata.' Sender, addressee and date of the biglietto not given. Not on DECODE. Manus gives the sheet-by-sheet description; the 29.114.a key sheets (Otto di Pratica, Dieci di Balia) are on the same fund and may fit. | Vetting 5 Nov 2026: leaf seen on the BNCF viewer (40x209 mm strip, four lines of symbol cipher, no gloss); held back from the catalogue until Lorenzo de Medici, Lettere VI (1481-82) is checked for a printed decipherment.
why: A short Medici cipher note of 1481 (Pazzi-war aftermath); cheap to test against the Florentine keys.
score_note: Scored from the Manus Online record description read on 4 Nov 2026 (research/sweep_2026-11_B_unswept_south/); not viewed
verify: Open the BNCF teca viewer, count the cipher lines, and try the Florentine chancery keys on DECODE (ASF) and Ginori Conti 29.114.a; compare Lorenzo de' Medici, Lettere.

vetting_note: Leaf seen, no gloss, but whether Lorenzo de' Medici, Lettere prints it is not settled. BNCF teca image BNCF0003827895 (c. 13r, 985x217, downloaded and enlarged 6 Nov 2026): a 40x209 mm strip, four full lines of symbol cipher, roughly 300 signs, with no sender, date, address or interlinear gloss; c. 13v holds only show-through and the BNCF stamp (inv. 3423197). Manus 611145 gives no sender, date or Lettere reference for it, though it cites Lettere for cc. 6-9 (VI p. 26) and cc. 20-21 (V p. 260). Google Books feed probes show the Censimento (1964) lists many Lorenzo pieces in 'BNF, GC, 137' with editor-assigned addressees and dates ('[Niccolo Michelozzi ?]' [giu. 1484 ?], [giu.] 1488, [dic. 1489]), and Lettere volumes cite GC 137 cc. 6-9, 20-21, 22-23/26/35, 34, 52-53; c. 13 was not found in the snippets, but the biglietto could be one of the bracketed Censimento items and printed, deciphered or not, in Lettere. Needs Chrome: https://www.google.com/books/edition/_/seEYGFQqM1kC?gbpv=1&bsq=GC,%20137 (Censimento) and the same bsq 'GC, 137, c. 13' in Lettere vols. title: Paderewski cabinet: notebook of enciphered telegrams on the internal situation in Poland (48 pp.)
status: Catalogue title: "Depesze szyfrowane dotyczace przede wszystkim sytuacji wewnetrznej w Polsce; (zeszyt)". Sibling of the June-Aug 1919 file 2/100/0/4.15/779 (lead 1892 in research/leads.json). No decipherment noted.
why: Same Warsaw-Paris cipher as file 779 over a second period; the two together give more text for one cipher.
score_note: Scored from the catalogue description during the Nov 2026 half-done runs sweep (research/sweep_2026-11_A_halfdone/); not viewed
verify: Request scans of 779 and 781 together; try the KNP cipher-section copies 2/39/0/2/256 (1919) as plaintext.
prior_art: open as far as checked (checked 4 Nov 2026: known.py on shelfmark and names, no hit apart from sibling lead 1892; Tomokiyo, Lasry, editions not searched)
vetting_note: No ciphertext shown and no scan: AAN 2/100/0/4.15/781 is not digitised ('Brak kopii cyfrowych'; the szukajwarchiwach detail page returned an empty JS shell to curl on 6 Nov 2026, so re-reading it needs Chrome: https://www.szukajwarchiwach.gov.pl/jednostka/-/jednostka/5335056). The title 'Depesze szyfrowane dotyczace przede wszystkim sytuacji wewnetrznej w Polsce; (zeszyt)' names cipher telegrams, but a 48-page exercise book is the usual form of a decrypt register, and the sibling file 779 (lead 1892, closed not_cipher on 3 Nov 2026 after all 100 frames were viewed) held only typed clear decrypts headed 'Telegram szyfrowy'. Prior art also open: the PISM edition Polskie Dokumenty Dyplomatyczne 1919 (July-December, ed. S. Debski) is built on the Paderewski archive and may print these telegrams; not opened. known.py on the shelfmark and Paderewski: only this lead, sibling 779 (lead 1892) and the 1940-41 Paderewski photocopies lead. Needs AAN scans of 781 to see whether it holds groups or clear text.
